construction.checkpoint: AES-256-GCM(K_cp; a Yjs full snapshot of the content root, AAD) — the snapshot includes row 8’s attribution records
construction.checkpoint_aad: LP("done/cp/v1") || LP(dec v) || LP(workspace_id) || LP(dec gen) || LP(dec epoch)
construction.manifest: Ed25519( producing credential ; LP("done/cp-manifest/v1") || LP(dec v) || LP(workspace_id) || LP(dec epoch) || LP(hex epoch_head) || LP(dec gen) || LP(hex checkpoint_digest) || LP(hex sv) || LP(hex ds) || LP(hex head_vector_digest) || LP(producing_credential) )
construction.head_vector: For each credential ascending by id: LP(credential_id) || LP(dec seq) || LP(hex link). Digest = SHA-256( LP("done/headvec/v1") || head_vector ). The sort is the canonicalization
construction.coverage: `sv` and `ds` bound separately, as opaque bytes. §7.6 forbids a bare state vector as a coverage claim; opacity means §10.1’s deferred Yjs upgrade changes what the bytes say rather than what this construction is
construction.attribution: Preserved by row 8 rather than by anything here. Each claim is signed by its own author and lives in the snapshotted content; the producer signs the container and nothing inside it, so §7.6’s forbidden shape is unreachable
cadence: A rotation forces a checkpoint under the new generation **before the old generation may be dropped** — a checkpoint is only openable while its generation is retained.

Otherwise: whichever comes first of an accepted-position count since the last checkpoint, or elapsed time. Both are tunables whose ground is first-sync cost (§12’s 1.5 s checkpoint verify), and neither can be set honestly before there is a service to measure.
retention: At least two checkpoints and their suffixes, because §11.3 test 8 requires falling back to the next-newest when the newest is unavailable.
Never drop a checkpoint whose generation is the newest one any retained checkpoint uses.

not_here.primitives: AES-256-GCM, HKDF, SHA-256 and Ed25519 KATs are row 1’s, in test/vectors/algorithm-suite.json.
not_here.attribution: The records inside the snapshot are row 8’s.
not_here.heads: The links and heads the vector collects are row 5’s.
not_here.packages: What a migration or terminal package carries is row 10’s.

producer.role: The credential that produced this checkpoint. It signs the container and nothing inside it.

other_credential.role: Another admitted credential, present so "produced by somebody else" is a vector rather than a sentence.

vectors.name: checkpoint-at-epoch-9
vectors.why: A laptop checkpointing a two-device workspace at epoch 9, generation 3. The snapshot includes row 8’s attribution records, which is what makes this preserve attribution without anyone re-signing anything.

inputs.snapshot_utf8: a Yjs full snapshot of the content root, including row 8’s attribution records

must_fail.name: coverage-ignores-deletions
must_fail.mutate: A manifest whose delete set differs while its state vector is identical. **This is §7.6’s stated failure as a vector**: two replicas can agree on `sv` and disagree about what has been deleted, so a bare state vector is not a coverage claim and `ds` has to be bound on its own.

must_fail.name: coverage-ignores-insertions
must_fail.mutate: The same manifest with a different state vector and the same delete set — the mirror of the negative above. Both halves are bound independently, so neither can be moved against the other, and the pair is published as a pair because §7.6’s point is that one of them alone is not a coverage claim.

must_fail.name: substituted-checkpoint-digest
must_fail.mutate: The manifest’s own digest field altered while the bytes beside it are untouched — a manifest pointing at a checkpoint nobody signed for. Distinct from `substituted-checkpoint`, which is the store’s keyless hash check: this is the signature, and only it survives a store that does not run the check.

must_fail.name: reordered-head-vector
must_fail.mutate: Serialize the accepted-head vector in insertion order rather than ascending by credential id. Isolates `head_vector_digest`, and the sort is what makes two devices checkpointing the same state agree.

must_fail.name: produced-by-another-credential
must_fail.mutate: A well-formed manifest signed by a different admitted credential. The producing credential is named in the message, so this fails on the binding and not only on the key.

must_fail.name: substituted-checkpoint
must_fail.mutate: A manifest paired with checkpoint bytes it does not digest. The durable store can check this without a content key, exactly as the relay checks an envelope’s digest (§7.2).

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace
must_fail.mutate: Verify the manifest against another workspace.

must_fail.name: wrong-generation
must_fail.mutate: Claim a generation the checkpoint was not sealed under. **A checkpoint is only openable while its generation is retained**, which is why rotation forces a new one before the old generation may be dropped.

must_fail.name: wrong-epoch
must_fail.mutate: Move the manifest to another epoch number.

must_fail.name: stale-epoch-head
must_fail.mutate: A current epoch number paired with an older head. Row 9’s pairing, applied to the artifact a recovering device reads first.

must_fail.name: wrong-version
must_fail.mutate: Claim manifest version 2 for a version-1 manifest.

must_fail.name: cp-aad-only-workspace
must_fail.mutate: Open the checkpoint as though it belonged to another workspace, subkey unchanged.

must_fail.name: cp-aad-only-version
must_fail.mutate: Open it claiming another format version.

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace-subkey
must_fail.mutate: Derive K_cp for another workspace. The AAD half is `cp-aad-only-workspace`.
